newsitem.title: UK: EU seen needing reform to compete in food markets.
newsitem.headline: EU seen needing reform to compete in food markets.

text.p: Current farm policies mean the EU will not be able to share in growth in world agricultural markets, the annual Oxford farm conference heard on Tuesday.

"If you in the EU maintain your current programmeit will block you from the world market if our price forecasts are right," said US expert Abner Womack who is a professor at the the University of Missouri-Columbia.
On the basis of US experience, Womack predicted a "glide down path," for EU farm supports. "It's not likely that quick change is politically possible," he said.
But with reform, the EU could be more successful. "If you do change your programmes it is very likely that you will become competitive in the world market," he said.
With the new Farm Bill, "the walls are down and the US is poised to respond quickly to the world market, Womack said.
The 1996 Farm Bill eliminates the US system of base acreage, which in the past has limited US farmers' capacity to respond to market changes, Womack said.
However, Womack's group at the Food and Agriculture Policy Research Institute assume a reduction in EU intervention prices for wheat after the year 2000.
Along with an increase in world prices this would make it possible for the EU to export wheat without the use of export subsidies.

Womack predicted increased pressure on the EU budget and external pressure on export subsidies, forcing sigificant sructural change in the EU. Farmers would receive less for commodities and there would be a gradual increase in farm size. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
